A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoFlow KV work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original implementation appendix B is retained as appendix F in v2; relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM and VLM benchmark results, positional ablations, retrieval and layer-selection analyses, and inference-latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, LongBench v2 results, attention-recovery measurements, a reordering ablation, and a latency breakdown.

M1.justification: Attention-mass top-k selection, global RoPE reconstruction, full-layer KV recomputation, and two-pass chunk reordering are retained. Section 4.3 makes the global selection budget, normalized chunk score, and tie handling explicit. Figure 1 already depicts reordering by selected-token ratio in v1, supporting clarification rather than an established algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds the LongBench v2 short-question subset, comprising 180 examples with reported context lengths of 10k-210k. The original four LongBench datasets, five VLM benchmarks, and Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluation remain. This extends coverage within the existing long-context QA focus.

E2.justification: Tables 7, 8, 10, and 11 add evaluated comparisons with KVLink5, TurboRAG, PCW, BM25 Recompute, PyramidKV, SnapKV, and StreamingLLM. This substantially broadens comparison beyond the original recomputation baselines to training-based cache reuse, retrieval, and compression or eviction methods.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a Llama-3-3B comparison, accuracy evaluation on the selected 180-example LongBench v2 subset, attention-matrix MSE averaged across layers on 100 HotpotQA examples, and an ascending-versus-descending ordering control. These substantially expand the evaluation protocol. Explicitly stating the existing experiments' 15% recomputation budget does not establish that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3, E, and G add tests of full-context attention recovery, sensitivity to chunk-order direction, and component-level runtime overhead. These provide substantial new mechanism and efficiency analyses. The original RoPE, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and layer-selection analyses remain; Figure 4's corrected caption does not constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report median latency over 10 independent runs. v2 adds no accuracy confidence intervals, significance tests, seed information, or revised repeated-run practice. The new evaluation sample counts and averaged metrics do not provide uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 7-14 add substantial results for new comparators, longer contexts, and diagnostic analyses. For example, Table 9 reports accuracy of 0.2889 for Our, 0.2611 for CacheBlend, and 0.2056 for EPIC. Among retained results, Table 3 changes the LLaMA fixed-chunk NarrativeQA baseline from 0.1623 to 0.1862. Most original scores remain unchanged; Table 6's conversion from percentages to fractions is equivalent.

T1.justification: The existing KV, RoPE, positional, and attention-selection mathematics is retained apart from notation clarification. Equation 9 expresses the selected-token-ratio reordering rule already depicted in v1 Figure 1. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion more explicitly center the contribution on multi-chunk KV reuse where full-context prefilling remains feasible but redundant. Information flow is qualified as operational rather than formal causal analysis. The central attention-selection, positional-alignment, and reordering contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially refines applicability and interpretation: it qualifies information-flow claims, limits the motivation when exact prefilling is already cheap, and distinguishes attention fidelity from generation-oriented selection. Section 6.3 corrects the VLM budget interpretation and acknowledges the OCRBench exception, 842 versus CacheBlend's 845 at k=2. Section 8 also frames latency comparisons as implementation-dependent measurements rather than ideal compute costs.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the common 15% recomputation budget, global first-stage selection without per-chunk quotas, normalized chunk scoring, and stable ordering of ties. It clarifies that VLM k denotes visual chunks and identifies FlashInfer-style kernels for irregular attention. These refine implementation and experiment documentation without establishing changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to SnapKV, KVLink, TurboRAG, and PCW, plus a RAG subsection explaining that the method operates after retrieval. Appendices B and D expand positioning relative to trained cache-reuse methods, passage retrieval, and complementary KV compression, while retaining the original training-free recomputation positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. v2 adds targeted explanations, revises terminology and section titles, updates author/affiliation and publication-header text, and reorganizes the expanded appendices, moving the original implementation appendix from B to F. This is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 7-14 substantially expand the presentation of comparisons and diagnostic evidence. Existing displays also change: Figure 2 receives new colors and marker styling, Tables 5-6 are restructured, and several captions and highlights are revised. Figure 4's erroneous heatmap caption is corrected while its actual plot remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central selection and efficiency claims through broader comparator families, attention-recovery and reversed-order controls, and longer-context evaluation. It also corrects misleading VLM interpretations and the Figure 4 caption, while clarifying application boundaries and experimental budgets. Some added baseline settings remain underspecified and accuracy uncertainty is still absent, but the targeted validation and correction of misleading explanations provide a substantial overall quality gain.
